## What it is

- The **TS808** came out in **1979**, designed by **Susumu Tamura** at Nisshin for Ibanez, with a **JRC4558** op-amp (Wikipedia, "Ibanez Tube Screamer").
- Three knobs: **Drive** (gain), **Tone** and **Level** (Wikipedia).
- It "boosts midrange frequencies and cuts bass" so a guitar stays clear in a band (Wikipedia, in other words).

## How it makes its sound

- The clipping stage is an op-amp with two diodes in its **feedback**. The diodes only let the extra (amplified) part grow to about 0.6 V; that is added to the clean signal. So it clips softly, and you still hear the note.
- In the feedback there is also a resistor and capacitor that only pass the **mids and highs** (a high-pass near 720 Hz in the schematic values this page uses, unverified). The low notes get almost no gain: the bass stays clean, the mids drive the diodes: the **mid hump**.
- Drive turns the gain from about 12 to about 118 times in this model. A small capacitor across the feedback cuts the highest treble more as Drive goes up.
- Players often put it in front of an already crunchy amp: it pushes the amp with the mids.

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="ts808" data-set="{&quot;drive&quot;:2,&quot;tone&quot;:5,&quot;level&quot;:8}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Drive 2.</b> A light edge. Listen how the low notes stay clean.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="ts808" data-set="{&quot;drive&quot;:8,&quot;tone&quot;:5,&quot;level&quot;:6}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Drive 8.</b> More clipping, still a clear note.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="ts808" data-set="{&quot;drive&quot;:8,&quot;tone&quot;:1,&quot;level&quot;:6}" data-play="lead"><p><b>Tone 1.</b> Darker: the tone stage's low-pass alone.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="ts808" data-set="{&quot;drive&quot;:8,&quot;tone&quot;:9,&quot;level&quot;:6}" data-play="lead"><p><b>Tone 9.</b> Brighter.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="ts808" data-set="{&quot;drive&quot;:5,&quot;tone&quot;:5,&quot;level&quot;:7}" data-play="chord"><p><b>A chord.</b> Compare with the Fuzz Face on the compare page: there the low strings fuzz too.</p></div>
```
